name: SiegeSurvivalSettings - Default (seed v1)
description: Survival (Defend the Castle) settings of a siege scenario: mode, teams, equipment, end conditions, spawning, stuck enemies and per-kill rewards. One per scenario.

steps.description: Which scenario plays as survival and who plays whom. A scenario without survival settings is an ordinary PvP siege.

fields.label: Scenario
fields.description: The siege scenario this belongs to; filled in from the scenario you are editing.

fields.label: Survival on
fields.description: Off keeps the survival settings but the scenario plays (and is listed) as ordinary PvP until it is on.

fields.label: Minimum players
fields.description: A survival match can start with this many players (default 1). The scenario's own PlayersMin keeps its PvP meaning.

fields.label: Human team
fields.description: The defender team the players join. Leave empty for the scenario's first Defender team.

fields.label: NPC team
fields.description: The attacker team the enemies belong to (no player ever joins it). Leave empty for the scenario's first Attacker team.

steps.description: How players are equipped (DESIGN §8): their own inventory, a kit picked at the hub, or a match loadout (Zombies-style). Purchase points, teammate transfers and the Mystery Box exist in every mode; inventories are kept on death everywhere.

fields.label: Equipment mode
fields.description: OwnInventory: players use their own gear. Kits: each player picks one of the selected kits at the hub. MatchProgression: players start with the baseline loadout (or an empty inventory).

fields.label: Default kit
fields.description: Kits mode: the kit a player who doesn't pick gets. Must be one of the selected kits.

fields.label: Baseline loadout
fields.description: Match progression: the kit granted at entry. Leave empty for an empty inventory.

steps.description: Kits mode: the kits players may pick at the hub. Save the settings first, then add kits with Create New Join Entry.

fields.label: Kits
fields.description: Each entry is a kit of the catalog.

steps.description: The pause between rounds, the end condition and the spawn preference (DESIGN §3a, §6).

fields.label: Pause between rounds (ms)
fields.description: The next round starts this long after the last enemy of a round died (default 10000 = 10 s). Dead players respawn at its start.

fields.label: End when all objectives are captured
fields.description: Off by default: then only a team wipe or an objective with Instant victory (insta-lose) ends the game. A survival lobby can override this.

fields.label: Favor spawning close to players (%)
fields.description: Share of the spawns that go to the active spawnzones nearest the living players (0-100); the rest is spread by zone weight. 0 = zone weight only. Never exclusive.

fields.label: Nearest zones
fields.description: How many of the nearest active zones count as 'close to the players' (default 1).

steps.description: Call of Duty-style stuck handling (DESIGN §3c): a stuck enemy is respawned closer to the players, the last enemies glow and chase, repeated respawns end in a system kill, and a round backstop clears what is left.

fields.label: Stuck after (ms)
fields.description: An enemy that made no progress for this long is respawned (default 30000).

fields.label: Last enemies
fields.description: When at most this many enemies of a round remain (and the queue is empty) they glow and go straight for the nearest player (default 3).

fields.label: Respawn limit
fields.description: An enemy respawned this many times and stuck again is killed by the system (default 2).

fields.label: Round backstop (ms)
fields.description: If the round is still running this long after its last planned enemy spawned, the rest is killed by the system (default 300000 = 5 min). Empty = off.

fields.label: Meaningful distance (blocks)
fields.description: Getting at least this much closer to the target counts as progress (default 1).

steps.description: Per NPC kill (DESIGN S32, S33): permanent coins and XP settled once at the end of a normal match, and match currency credited at once. Headshot and critical-hit kills pay the bonus multiplier.

fields.label: Coins per kill
fields.description: Permanent coins per kill. Leave empty for the scenario's capture coin reward ÷ 10.

fields.label: XP per kill
fields.description: Permanent experience per kill. Leave empty for the scenario's capture XP reward ÷ 10.

fields.label: Match currency per kill
fields.description: Spendable match currency per kill (default 70); it only exists inside the match.

fields.label: Headshot / critical multiplier
fields.description: Multiplier for a headshot or critical-hit kill (default 1.1), applied once.
